newsitem.title: USA: U.S. would take new N.Korea food appeal seriously.
newsitem.headline: U.S. would take new N.Korea food appeal seriously.

text.p: The United States said on Monday it would consider "very seriously" any new U.N. food appeal for North Korea and urged other countries also to contribute because the Stalinist state is facing a famine.

Washington has not been asked for any more food aid by the U.N. World Food Programme (WFP) beyond $25 million recently donated, but if another appeal is made "we would look at it very, very seriously," State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said.

Asked about reports that Japan and South Korea, among other countries, have not responded to a WFP appeal several weeks ago for $95.5 million in food aid, Burns said: "We do hope that other countries will respond favourably ... we think that one ought to separate politics from humanitarian need."

The WFP on Monday called for large scale emergency aid to North Korea to prevent a famine that executive director Catherine Bertini said could turn into "one of the biggest humanitarian disasters of our lifetime."
Bertini's statement did not, however, appear to represent a formal new appeal.

Burns said the United States agreed that "there is a famine in North Korea." Two ships carrying U.S. grain in response to an earlier WFP appeal are due to arrive in the North Korean port of Nampo on May 4 and 12, he noted.
The United States and South Korea met North Korea in New York nearly two weeks ago to hear Pyongyang's response to U.S.-South Korea proposals for peace talks.
North Korean negotiators said Pyongyang was willing to enter into the peace talks but conditioned its participation on more food aid, lifting U.S. trade sanctions and diplomatic recognition.

Commenting on television footage of a North Korean military parade last Friday, Burns called North Korea an "over-militarized country" that needed to pay more attention to the needs of its civilian population.
"It would seem to us that those well-fed soldiers and well-groomed soldiers with brilliant uniforms, some of that money ought to be spent on their own people who are starving," he said.
